About.title: Write DESIGN.md, then put it to work
About.intro: RICOUI DESIGN is a local-first workspace for DESIGN.md. It brings editing, checks, previews, and exports together so a design specification can keep evolving after handoff.
About.betaTitle: The product is still taking shape
About.betaDetail: RICOUI DESIGN is ready for everyday editing and export, but its interactions, format support, and cloud features are still being refined. Feedback from real use will shape what comes next.
About.openSourceTitle: The project, its source, and its documentation
About.openSourceDetail: RICOUI DESIGN is developed in the open. The repository includes the application source, configuration examples, and guides for using, deploying, and contributing to the project.
About.repositoryDetail: Source code, issues, and ongoing updates
About.guideDetail: Usage, AI, sync, deployment, and contribution
About.profileDetail: RicoUI is my personal brand. At ricoui.com, I share work and notes on design, code, and creative practice.
About.focusTitle: Make design specifications easier to understand and maintain.
About.focusWebTitle: Start with a readable source file

About.focusCodeDetail: The same content can be edited, checked, and exported as tokens and CSS, reducing the gap between design guidance and implementation.
About.focusCreateTitle: Tools should leave room for judgment
About.focusCreateDetail: Parsing and AI can help, but the source file, editing decisions, and final result stay under the user's control.

RicoUI is my personal brand for sharing design, code, and creative work; RICOUI DESIGN is one project within it.

faqs.q1: Is data uploaded to a server automatically?
faqs.a1: No. Data is stored in browser IndexedDB by default. A personal workspace participates in cloud sync only after Supabase is configured and you sign in.
faqs.q2: Does AI read a document when I open the panel?
faqs.a2: No. Content is sent only when you explicitly run analysis or standardization, and changes must be previewed before they are applied.
faqs.q3: Why do I see format diagnostics after importing?
faqs.a3: The editor parses DESIGN.md using expected sections and tables. Unknown content is preserved, but structured editing cannot build a complete mapping when key tables are missing.
faqs.q4: What is the difference between the brand library and my library?
faqs.a4: The brand library contains read-only references. Your library contains assets you save, classify, and maintain. Copy brand content into a draft before editing it.
faqs.q5: Does preview.html drive the in-app preview?
faqs.a5: No. The in-app preview is always parsed from DESIGN.md. preview.html is a standalone deliverable that can be opened or downloaded separately.
faqs.q6: Why was cloud sync paused, and what should I do?
faqs.a6: When another device has updated the same document, the editor keeps saving your current work on this device but pauses cloud upload for that document. Open “Compare and resolve” to use the local version in cloud, load the cloud version, or explicitly save a new draft. The app does not create conflict copies automatically.
faqs.q7: Why does GLM keep processing without returning text?
faqs.a7: GLM models can return reasoning separately from visible text. The editor disables Thinking for standardization, assistant, repair, and analysis tasks, and reports an error if a response ends without visible text. Coding Plan is an experimental compatibility option because its endpoint is officially intended for listed coding tools; for stable access, use the standard Z.AI / GLM API. Error 1305 means the service is busy, not that your API key is invalid.
faqs.q8: Can regular Markdown be saved to the library?
faqs.a8: Yes. Any non-empty Markdown can be saved and its source is preserved in full. Regular Markdown is marked Source only; recognized design structure enables structured editing and preview; JSON, CSS, ZIP, and delivery versions become available only after token and value checks pass.

create.label: Create a draft
create.title: Create and import your first DESIGN.md
create.outcome: A locally autosaved draft that the structured editor can parse.
create.s1b: Open the workspace and select New draft. Start with the standard blank template or copy from the library or brand library.
create.s2b: Select Import and upload one or more .md files. A single successful file opens immediately; batch results show an import summary.
create.s3b: The editor identifies color, typography, spacing, and component sections. Unknown blocks remain unchanged, and format risks appear in diagnostics.
create.s4b: Rename it, pin frequently used documents, or add categories and tags. Content changes are saved locally in the browser.

edit.label: Edit tokens
edit.title: Edit tokens and validate the live preview
edit.outcome: An understanding of how source, reading, structured, and preview views stay in sync.
edit.s1b: Switch between source and reading views to confirm the Markdown sections and table structure.
edit.s2b: Open structured view and edit colors, fonts, type steps, spacing, or radii. Controls rewrite only the corresponding modeled block.
edit.s3b: The preview is generated from the current DESIGN.md. If the source becomes invalid, the last valid result remains visible.
edit.s4b: Use the toolbar to export DESIGN.md, DTCG tokens.json, variables.css, or Tailwind theme.css.

library.label: Save to library
library.title: Preserve source and unlock derivatives by capability
library.outcome: A library entry that preserves the complete Markdown source and states its current capability level.
library.s1b: Open the target draft in the workspace and select Save to library.
library.s2b: Use the name for identification, description for purpose, category for primary ownership, and tags for style and technical traits.
library.s3b: The first save creates an entry. A draft created from the library can update its source or save as a new version.
library.s4b: Source-only entries always support viewing, copying, and downloading Markdown. Recognized design structure enables preview and structured editing; valid tokens then enable JSON, CSS, ZIP, and delivery versions.

ai.label: AI assistance
ai.title: Analyze and standardize documents safely
ai.outcome: A read-only analysis or candidate standardized version without automatic changes to the source.
ai.s1b: Add an OpenAI-compatible provider, API key, and model in Settings. Credentials remain on this device.
ai.s2b: Open the AI workspace from the editor. Opening the panel alone sends no document and makes no model request.
ai.s3b: Analysis provides read-only suggestions; standardization generates a candidate. Both require an explicit action.
ai.s4b: Compare the current source with the candidate. The draft changes only after you select Apply.
